ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: 11.6 km actually driven against a 9.8 km recommended route is a deviation of 1.80 km, well outside the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. This is not a within-tolerance trip that can be waved through.

The GPS trace corroborates which route was taken and when, exactly the use POL-RD-22 permits: the map-matched fixes run on Upper Bukit Timah Road and Bukit Timah Road to 18:44:00, move onto Holland Road from 18:44:30, continue via Napier Road, and only rejoin the recommended line on Kim Seng Road at about 18:58. The diversion is a real, mapped detour, not a measurement artefact.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The only traffic record in the case is LTA advisory LTA-TI-260914-6951, a road closure on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road, and its active window is 00:30 to 05:30 on 14 September 2026. This trip ran from 18:29 to 19:00 that evening. The advisory's window does not overlap the trip window, so POL-RD-23's requirement of a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route AND overlaps the trip window is not met.

POL-RD-23 is express that a driver's assertion of traffic, with no such data for the recommended segment at the trip time, does not justify the reroute. That is this case: the closure on the record had ended about thirteen hours before the trip; the trace shows the vehicle moving along Bukit Timah Road at reported speeds of 19 to 32 km/h up to the deviation point, consistent with a road that was open and flowing; and the rider's statement on file is that the road was open and moving. The driver's 'LTA announced it, so I took Holland Road' cannot supply the justification the advisory withholds.

The facts select POL-RD-24(d): the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, 1.80 km at 0.72 SGD/km, which the fare ledger itself carries as excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.30; and the ledger shows exactly that 1.30 already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 1.30), matching the trip record's fare_adjusted event. The matrix sends that money to the rider, not back to the driver.

No row of the POL-RD-24 matrix yields a payment to the driver. Rows (a) and (c) both require traffic justification, which the advisory defeats; rows (b) and (d) direct the excess distance fare to the rider; and row (e) is unavailable because the deviation is over 1 km. The driver's claim to have the 1.30 SGD restored to him therefore finds no row of the matrix to stand on.

I do not dispute the notification limb. The driver's in-app message at 18:41:22 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?') preceded the departure from the recommended line at 18:44, and the rider answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, so on POL-RD-21's terms the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment.

Notification and acknowledgment do not carry the driver into row (a). Row (a) requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as informed and agreed, and POL-RD-24's not-justified branch contains no information element at all: row (d) turns on justification and distance alone. The rider's 'ok sure' was in any event given in answer to the driver's assertion that the road was closed, a premise the traffic record contradicts for the trip time, so it cannot be treated as an informed agreement to a reroute the driver had no traffic basis for.

This dispute is for the AI to decide, not to escalate: the contested amount is 1.30 SGD, far below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence subject only to POL-RD-25's 0.80 floor, which COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 support; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so no raised confidence threshold applies; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in this policy version (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false), so the 1.80 km deviation does not take the case out of AI decision.

The driver satisfied POL-RD-21 on this record. He sent the rider an in-app chat at 18:41:22 — before the route deviation detected at 18:44:22 — with the brief reason the clause requires ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?'); the rider read it (read_at 18:42:30) and replied 'ok sure' at 18:41:47. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and that is exactly what this log shows.

The only traffic artifact in the record names a ROAD_CLOSURE on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road and prescribes 'Diversion via Holland Rd' — the very recommended corridor the driver left at 18:44:22 and the very alternate he took, the GPS fixes placing the vehicle on Holland Road from 18:44:30. The driver's account therefore tracks LTA's own published corridor and diversion, while the rider's denial that any closure was announced is supported by nothing in the record. I do not overstate it: the advisory's active window (00:30–05:30) does not overlap the trip window (18:34–19:00), so POL-RD-23's strict data test is not met on its face, and this artifact's force is corroboration of the driver's good faith rather than a dispositive justification.

The rider's counterparty statement — that the road was open and that she agreed 'only because he said it was closed' — is a bare assertion made the morning after the refund. The contemporaneous chat log carries admissibility weight 1.0 with no issue codes, is complete and untruncated, and records an unqualified 'ok sure' given after she had read the driver's specific question. Under POL-RD-21 the acknowledgment the chat log carries governs whether the deviation was agreed, and the rider's later, uncorroborated denial does not displace it.

On any view of the matrix the driver's exposure is capped, and it has already been met. POL-RD-24 provides exactly one refund where a deviation is not traffic-justified and exceeds tolerance — the excess distance fare — which here is the deviation of 1.80 km (POL-RD-22: recorded actual 11.6 km minus recommended 9.8 km) times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, with no surge applied: 1.30 SGD. That is precisely the figure already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so nothing further can lawfully be taken from him, and neither POL-RD-24 nor any other clause permits any part of the trip fare itself, or any larger sum, to be recovered.

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 1.30, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 2 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 1.30, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 3 (sampled): NO_ACTION, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 4 (position_swapped): NO_ACTION, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
At most 2 of 4 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
